summary: Code review PASS. All three TypeScript files are clean and idiomatic. DIALOGUES_DIR constant is well-placed and typed. GuiConfigSchema/DEFAULT_CONFIG changes are minimal and correct. GuiConfigPartialSchema auto-inheritance pattern is robust. 20/20 tests pass. No blocking issues, no fix-forwards needed.

comments.note: No blocking issues. DIALOGUES_DIR is correctly placed alongside PLAN_ARCHIVE_FILENAME/SYNTHESIS_ARCHIVE_FILENAME — a cohesive constants section for all archive-path literals. The 'dialogues' as const typing ensures TypeScript literal inference for consumers.

GuiConfigPartialSchema auto-inheritance via omit-then-partial is architecturally sound: new writable fields like capture_dialogues are automatically included in the partial schema without explicit changes. This is a well-designed extensibility pattern that reduces future churn.

The writeConfig round-trip test for capture_dialogues: false seeds the value as true first before writing false — this correctly proves the false value is actively persisted rather than being a default pass-through. Thorough test design.

The DIALOGUES_DIR constant is used by both the Python orchestrator (write_dialogue()) and the MCP server. This cross-language coupling is documented in the JSDoc comment in constants.ts, but the Documentation agent should consider adding a cross-reference note in the orchestrator's dialogue_writer.py docstring (or a shared architecture doc) to make this linkage discoverable from both sides.
